standards_review.notes: Only 1 of 13 commit subjects in the review range matches the documented 'EPMCDME-####: Description' format (git-workflow.md); the rest (e.g. 'sonarlint fixes', 'fixed unittests.', 'gitleaks', 'fixes after rebase.', 'Refactor LLMService and ProjectService authorization checks for clarity') carry no ticket prefix.

code-quality.md requires 'X | None' unions and parameterized generics (list[str], dict[str,str]) in new code, not typing.Optional/List/Dict. New/changed lines use Optional[...] and List[...]/Dict[...] throughout src/codemie/service/llm_service/llm_service.py (e.g. lines 34,56,78,109,250,279-280,333-334), src/codemie/rest_api/routers/projects.py (new AllowedModelsUpdateRequest/Response and ProjectDetailResponse fields, e.g. lines 17-49), and src/codemie/rest_api/routers/llm_models.py (get_project_from_id and get_llm_models params, lines 42,61,113); llm_models.py also reverts the existing 'from __future__ import annotations' back to 'from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union'.

security-patterns.md names 'Inline role checks with inconsistent messages' as the anti-pattern vs. using admin/maintainer/project-admin helper dependencies. New ProjectService.check_allowed_models_authorization (src/codemie/service/project/project_service.py) reimplements authorization inline as 'user.is_admin or (up and up.is_project_admin)', omitting the maintainer check even though its own docstring and ERRORS.ALLOWED_MODELS_UNAUTHORIZED message both claim 'Only project admins and maintainers can update this field'. Every other mutating endpoint in the same file (src/codemie/rest_api/routers/projects.py) authorizes via the shared `_authorize_project_access` dependency or the existing `user.is_admin_or_maintainer` helper (line 1064); the new PATCH /projects/{projectName}/allowed-models endpoint bypasses that shared pattern entirely.
